# [STORY] As a platform operator, I want config-service to actually deliver configuration in the Docker profile, so that the Spring Cloud Config setup works as ADR-005 describes

## User Story
**As a** platform operator
**I want** config-service to actually deliver configuration in the Docker profile
**So that** the Spring Cloud Config setup behaves the way ADR-005 describes, instead of being wired up but inert

## Acceptance Criteria (Given/When/Then)
- [x] Given the Docker profile is running, when a service starts, then it loads its configuration from config-service rather than silently skipping it
- [x] Given a served config file is emptied or deleted, when the config-service test suite runs, then it fails
- [x] Given the Kubernetes overlays (local/minikube, aws, azure), when they are rendered and a service starts, then nothing changes — config-service stays undeployed per ADR-005
- [ ] Given a request to a path the config server does not recognise, when it is served, then the response is not a misleading HTTP 200

## Definition of Ready
- [x] Meets [Definition of Ready](https://github.com/liviuionesi/lmdb.dev/blob/develop/docs/process/DEFINITION_OF_READY.md)

## Story Points
**Estimate:** 5

## Sprint
**Milestone:** Sprint 8

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Meets [Definition of Done](https://github.com/liviuionesi/lmdb.dev/blob/develop/docs/process/DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md)

## Notes
ADR-005 keeps Eureka and Config Server in the Docker/bare-JVM profile only.
Kubernetes uses cluster DNS plus ConfigMaps and Secrets. This Story does not
change that split — it makes the Docker half true.
